analysis:
This PR changes documentation only: docs/architecture/telemetry.md (head lines 34-43 add an Autopilot busy-reasons section) and docs/reference/protocol-messages.md (a status `detail` field, a command `hold_seconds` field, consent-gated state fields `capabilities`, `adopted_models`, `held_models`, `busy_reasons`, `busy_reason`, `busy_since_ms` and `transition_stalls`, and closed vocabularies). No executable code, auth, crypto or attestation logic is modified.

Security-relevant observations on the documented contract:
- The new heartbeat fields are consent-gated, additive, and drawn from closed vocabularies. They expose provider-state metadata (busy cause, stall counts, held model IDs) to the coordinator. The coordinator is already trusted and sees model residency, so this adds no consumer-facing or prompt-content disclosure (A-001). The text states the fields carry no prompt content and are typed heartbeat fields, not event emissions.
- `hold_seconds` and adopted inventory are coordinator-issued command inputs and are bounded (0..86400). They are documented as affecting only LRU eviction and idle unload, not authorization. They are honoured only when the provider reports `placement_holds`, so a coordinator cannot rely on them otherwise. This is a resource-availability concern at most (T-029 style), is bounded, and sits in the trusted coordinator-to-provider direction.
- The docs claim older coordinators ignore unknown keys, citing coordinator/protocol/messages.go at an immutable platform revision (f512258...). That is an external contract I could not verify. If it is wrong, the impact is registration or heartbeat decode failure, which is an availability issue. I record it as an unverified contract rather than a finding.
- Docs state `protocol` stays 3 and that adoption and holds are relied on only after a matching capability is reported. The platform enforcement of that is outside the supplied evidence.
- The patch excerpt for protocol-messages.md is truncated and the referenced model-autopilot.md anchor is not supplied, so I could not review the 'busy-reasons-and-stalled-transitions' architecture text.

No regression or threat-model invalidation identified.
